issue.title: FR: use different style when showing multiple files, one file, (maybe) piped input

relevant_locations.role: Defines the command-line arguments including the '--style' option.

llm_context.input_title: FR: use different style when showing multiple files, one file, (maybe) piped input
llm_context.input_body: No body provided in issue description.

generated_output.summary: The user wants to dynamically customize the output style of 'bat' based on the context of the inputs: specifically, using a simpler style (like plain) for a single file or stdin, and a richer style (like grid/header) when displaying multiple files. Currently, 'bat' only supports a single global style configuration.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: The command-line interface defined in 'src/bin/bat/clap_app.rs' only defines the '--style' option. In 'src/bin/bat/app.rs', the 'style_components' method resolves the active style components solely based on the '--style' argument, '--decorations', or '--plain' flags, without any knowledge of or reference to the number of files or input types (stdin vs. regular files) being processed.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect Control Flow and Style Resolution
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect `src/bin/bat/clap_app.rs` to see how `--style` is defined, and inspect `src/bin/bat/app.rs` (specifically the `style_components` method) to understand how style components are currently resolved from the parsed arguments.

step_by_step_plan.title: Define New Command-Line Options
step_by_step_plan.description: Add `--style-single-file`, `--style-multiple-files`, and `--style-stdin` options to the clap application definition in `src/bin/bat/clap_app.rs` under the style-related arguments section.

step_by_step_plan.title: Update Style Resolution Logic
step_by_step_plan.description: Modify the `style_components` method in `src/bin/bat/app.rs` to accept the list of inputs or their count/type. Implement logic to check if `--style-single-file`, `--style-multiple-files`, or `--style-stdin` are provided, and override the default style based on whether there is a single file, multiple files, or stdin being processed.

step_by_step_plan.title: Add Integration Tests and Verify
step_by_step_plan.description: Create integration tests in the existing test suite that execute `bat` with different combinations of inputs (single file, multiple files, stdin) and the new style override flags, asserting that the correct output decorations are rendered. Run `cargo test` to verify.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: A design pattern where more specific configuration options override more general ones based on runtime context.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: It allows command-line tools to have sensible, broad defaults while giving advanced users fine-grained control over specific scenarios without needing wrapper scripts.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Implementing '--style-single-file' and '--style-multiple-files' requires cascading these specific style overrides over the base '--style' configuration depending on the runtime input count.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: The ability of a CLI application to inspect its input sources (such as files vs. standard input) and count them before rendering output.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: It enables tools to adapt their user interface dynamically, such as hiding headers when there is only one stream to display.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: The application needs to count the parsed inputs and check if any are stdin to decide which style override to apply.

common_pitfalls: Modifying the core 'pretty_printer' library to handle these CLI-specific style overrides. The style resolution logic should remain in the CLI application layer ('src/bin/bat/app.rs').

Failing to handle the mixed input corner case (e.g., 'echo qq | bat - filename'), where multiple files are present but one of them is stdin. The multiple-files style should take precedence here to keep the output consistent.
Breaking the existing '--style=auto' behavior or ignoring the 'BAT_STYLE' environment variable.
